name: UKFRS FG1
label: UK FRS Fireground 1 General incident
source_title: NFCC Fireground Radios Guidance (Grenfell Inquiry exhibit CWJ00000114)
notes: National UK-wide simplex assignment licensed by Ofcom to FRS. NFCC states regulations require clear speech (not encrypted). DMR is the post-2017 recommended primary; analogue remains for interoperability. NFCC standard DMR codeplug uses colour code 1 timeslot 1 and group ID 901 (talkgroup_id left blank for promiscuous monitor use). Original URL 301s to the UK Government Web Archive.

name: HMCG Ch16
label: HM Coastguard / international distress safety and calling Ch 16
source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK
notes: ITU Appendix 18 / GMDSS voice distress safety and calling. MCA MGN 324 Amendment 2 states Channel 16 is 156.8 MHz. Analogue FM radiotelephony; unencrypted by design. Channel 70 DSC is not recorded (not FM voice).

name: HMCG Ch67
label: HM Coastguard yacht safety / first-reserve SAR Ch 67
source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK
notes: Ofcom: communication between ship aircraft and land stations in coordinated SAR and anti-pollution; also HMCG Yacht safety channel (1st reserve). MCA FOI 01497978 lists 156.375 MHz as International VHF Ch 67 licensed to the MCA.

name: HMCG Ch73
label: HM Coastguard second-reserve SAR Ch 73
source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK

name: HMCG Ch10
label: HM Coastguard coordinated SAR / anti-pollution Ch 10
source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK
notes: Ofcom: ship/aircraft/land SAR and anti-pollution. MCA Advice Note 1033 also allows VHF Channel 10 for MSI broadcasts to reduce interference.

name: HMCG Ch6
label: Ship-aircraft coordinated SAR Ch 6
source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK
notes: Ofcom: communications between ship stations and aircraft stations engaged in coordinated SAR. MCA FOI lists 156.300 MHz as International VHF Ch 6.

name: HMCG Ch13
label: GMDSS navigation-safety / bridge-to-bridge Ch 13
source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK
notes: Ofcom lists 156.65 MHz for GMDSS ship-to-ship safety-of-navigation. MCA MGN 324 designates Channel 13 worldwide as a navigation-safety channel.

name: HMCG UK156

source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK

name: RNLI Ch31
label: RNLI Channel 31 lifeboat to shore crew
source_title: Ofcom: Frequencies for distress and safety search and rescue and emergencies in the UK
notes: Ofcom auxiliary SAR table: Channel 31 used for lifeboat to shore crew communications during launch and recovery (and may be used farther out to sea). Bandwidth not explicitly stated; 25 kHz recorded because Ofcom gives a 25 kHz-raster maritime centre frequency. CTCSS not documented. RNLI crew-alerting/paging on 153.075 MHz is not recorded (not documented as FM voice).
